name: Proverbs

objectives.text: Identify Proverbs as a book in the Old Testament that gives wise sayings for everyday life
Recall that King Solomon asked God for wisdom and wrote many proverbs
Recall proverbs that teach children to listen to the instruction of their father and mother
Describe the difference between a wise person and a fool using examples from Proverbs
Explain what Proverbs means when it teaches that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom
Compare the sluggard with the ant to explain what Proverbs teaches about diligent work
Explain the difference between knowledge and wisdom as Proverbs presents them
Apply proverbs about speech and anger to everyday situations in class role plays or case studies
Classify two-line proverbs as synonymous, antithetic, or comparative parallelism
Outline the main collections of Proverbs using the headings that introduce each section
Analyze how chapters 1 to 9 alternate between a father's instruction to his son and the speeches of Woman Wisdom
Compare the invitations of Woman Wisdom with the warnings against the adulterous woman and Woman Folly
Analyze why proverbs are read as general observations of how life ordinarily works rather than unconditional promises
Explain how Proverbs connects wisdom with the order God built into creation
Explain how Proverbs teaches that the Lord governs human plans and their outcomes
Analyze how Proverbs ties wisdom to righteousness and to keeping God's law
Construct a topical study that traces a theme such as wealth, speech, or friendship across the collections of Proverbs
Explain how New Testament writers quote and apply passages from Proverbs
Compare the sayings of the wise in Proverbs with Ancient Near Eastern wisdom such as the Instruction of Amenemope
Evaluate interpretations of the personified Wisdom of Proverbs 8, including the church's reading in light of Christ as the wisdom of God
Analyze the acrostic poem of the excellent wife as a portrait of wisdom lived out that echoes Woman Wisdom
Evaluate how the teaching of Proverbs applies to contemporary moral questions when read alongside the rest of Scripture

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (book identity, Solomon, listening to parents, wise vs fool, fear of the Lord, knowledge vs wisdom, sluggard and ant, speech and anger, chapters 1 to 9 structure, proverbs as general truths, wisdom and creation, Woman Folly, topical study, Proverbs 8, Proverbs 31, modern ethics). Replaced vague 'defend practical value' with an evaluation tied to Scripture as a whole. Added parallelism forms, the book's collections, God's sovereignty over plans, wisdom and the law, New Testament use of Proverbs, and Ancient Near Eastern comparison. Added verse-level references and confession anchors where they state the doctrine.
